description:
Context
Dedicated customers are increasingly asking for contractual/operational guardrails on autoscaling: explicit min/max bounds to control spend and preserve baseline capacity, plus an optional predictive mode to avoid cold-start/queue buildup during known ramps (time-of-day patterns, scheduled events). Today, scaling behavior is mostly platform-driven (reactive signals + operator overrides) and is insufficiently deterministic/auditable for enterprise.

Problem statements (customer-facing)
1) “We need a hard max to prevent unexpected scale-up spend.”
2) “We need a hard minimum to meet latency SLOs at all times, including after deploys and during warm-up.”
3) “We can predict our daily ramp—can Redwood pre-scale to avoid queueing?”
4) “We need an audit trail of who changed scaling settings and why the system scaled.”

Scope (this epic)
- Customer-configurable autoscaling bounds: hard min/max replicas (and/or GPU quota) per Dedicated deployment; clear precedence over platform defaults.
- Predictive scaling signals: forecast-informed biasing of desired capacity with deterministic arbitration against reactive signals; always respect bounds.
- Safety + reliability: anti-oscillation guardrails (cooldowns, dampening, min step sizing), and deterministic behavior under conflicting signals.
- Operability: dashboards, alerts, and runbooks; auditability for config changes + scaling decisions.
- Customer experience: bounds + predictive mode exposed in Console/API (+ Terraform support), docs semantics, CS/support playbooks.

Out of scope (initial GA)
- Cross-region active-active predictive placement optimization.
- Dynamic contract renegotiation workflows.
- Fully automated procurement based on forecasts.

Milestone tracking (definition of done per phase)
Phase 0 (Discovery)
- Confirm min/max semantics customers expect (hard vs soft) and document default behavior for existing deployments.
- Identify pilot customers + success criteria.

Phase 1 (Design)
- Finalize schema fields (min/max, cooldowns, predictive toggle, fallback behaviors), including validation rules.
- ADR approved: precedence ordering, safety invariants, conflict resolution reactive vs predictive, deterministic audit fields.
- Observability plan reviewed: metrics naming, cardinality limits, dashboards + alert thresholds.

Phase 2 (Build)
- Control plane API & persistence: create/update/read policy with RBAC + validation; migration/backfill for existing Dedicated deployments.
- Autoscaler enforcement: compute requested desired, then clamp to bounded desired; emit bound-hit metrics and decision reasons.
- Predictive integration: forecast provider interface, staleness checks, fall back to reactive scaling; anti-oscillation guardrails.
- Audit logging: config change events + scaling decision events with enough context for enterprise compliance.
- Simulation harness: replay historical traces to compare reactive-only vs predictive; document results and acceptance thresholds.

Phase 3 (Pilot)
- Canary in one region; enable per-account feature flag + per-deployment enablement.
- SRE readiness review complete (alerts tested, paging routes verified, game day executed).
- Pilot check-ins weekly; track incidents, false positives/negatives, oscillation; iterate on guardrails.

Phase 4 (GA)
- Docs + release notes published; CS macros/playbooks ready.
- GA checklist complete; go/no-go approved; monitoring plan in place.

Notes
- Determinism requirement: every scaling tick must record requested desired (by signal), bounded desired, and reason(s) for clamp/override.
- Invariant: never exceed max; never go below min (unless region shortage prevents provisioning—in which case surface “min unmet” degraded state and alert).
- Backward compatibility: no behavior change for existing Dedicated deployments until feature-flag enabled and policy set/confirmed.
ga_exit_criteria:
GA exit criteria (must meet all unless explicitly waived by exec sponsors Priya Natarajan / Neha Kapoor)

Correctness & semantics
- Bounds are hard-enforced in autoscaler loop: bounded_desired is always within [min,max] for enabled deployments.
- Predictive mode is additive and deterministic: reactive safety signals can override prediction (within bounds), with explicit decision reason logged.
- Null/stale forecast never causes unsafe downscale; forecast staleness triggers fallback to reactive-only.
- Validation complete: min <= max, cooldowns within supported ranges, rate-limited config updates to prevent churn.

Reliability & SLOs
- No statistically significant regression in Dedicated p95 latency attributable to scaling for enabled customers over a 2-week canary window (compare control vs enabled).
- Max-bound saturation and sustained queue buildup are detectable via alerts with acceptable noise (alert runbook tested).
- Region shortage behavior: “min unmet” state is visible in Console + surfaced to on-call; customer comms template available.

Observability & operability
- Dashboards include: desired vs bounded replicas, bound-hit rate, queue depth, saturation signals, scale event timeline, prediction vs actual demand, prediction error.
- On-call runbook updated and reviewed by SRE; game day completed (forecast outage, spike, stuck scale-down, max-bound saturation scenarios).

Auditability & compliance
- Audit events emitted for (a) policy changes (who/when/what) and (b) scaling decisions (requested desired, bounded desired, reason codes, signal inputs summary).
- Retention meets enterprise requirements; export path documented for customers who require audit log ingestion.

Customer readiness
- Console UX shipped with clear messaging: effective policy, recommended ranges, warnings on risky settings, and explanation of predictive mode limitations.
- Terraform support available for enterprise IaC workflows (module/provider examples + docs).
- CS playbook and predictive known-issues doc published; Support macros prepared.

Rollout controls
- Feature-flag gating per account and per deployment; safe rollback path proven (disable predictive mode first, then disable policy enforcement gating if needed).
- GA announcement and release notes ready; internal escalation path defined (Support -> TAM -> SRE -> Infra on-call).
